results.visibleTextIdentical: PASS — 24,964 characters, equal after stripping style/script bodies, tags and decoding entities
results.everyDeletedByteAccountedFor: PASS — the 93 bytes are exactly ` \n `, i.e. the empty span the build-time translation left behind when it emptied the QA note

compositionComparison.myPreRegisteredClaimWasFalsified: CP1's challenge #6 pre-registered 'byte-identical, including the entities'. It is NOT byte-identical and that claim is withdrawn rather than quietly dropped. The first run differed by 99 bytes and a second difference was mine, not the translation's: I had emitted a literal `·` where the translation emits `·`. That was corrected in the generator, which reduced the delta to the irreducible 93 bytes of the emptied span. No recorded hash or size of the composed document exists anywhere in the repo, so no claim elsewhere depends on the old hash.
compositionComparison.whatTheDifferenceIsNot: It is not text, not a figure, and not a citation. The pre-fix document already rendered that span empty. The span was a flex item in a `display:flex` row with `gap`, and removing it lets the adjacent `flex:1` spacer absorb the freed gap, so the visible row is laid out identically. The stated claim is now the measured one: the reader's document is unchanged in every rendered character, and the byte difference is one empty element with zero rendered size.
compositionComparison.guardStillHolds: `_design/bastrop-review/build.mjs` composes both copies with exit 0, so its own `BANNED` refusal list still passes on the fixed boards — the translation being inert does not break the send-safety guard.
